text: Research suggests that direct associative conditioning is often responsible for the development of dental fear [ 13 – 15 ]. That is, an individual who undergoes an uncomfortable or painful dental procedure (unconditioned stimulus) may form an association between the dentist and/or dental-related stimuli (the conditioned stimulus) with fear (the conditioned response). In subsequent situations, such as future dental consultations, the dentist and/or dental related stimuli will then elicit the conditioned response.
source_label: A test of pre-exposure spacing and multiple context pre-exposure on the mechanisms of latent inhibition of dental fear: A study protocol
